pulse_posts.title: Why Composite B-Tree Indexes Fail Silently in High-Write PostgreSQL Workloads
pulse_posts.body:
When optimizing slow SQL queries, junior engineers often add single-column indexes on every WHERE clause column. In production, column order inside a composite index (Leftmost Prefix Rule) dictates whether the query planner performs an Index Seek or falls back to a Sequential Scan.

Rule of thumb for your next architecture review: place equality predicates (=) first, and range predicates (>, <, BETWEEN) last.

pulse_posts.mentor_headline: VP of Corporate Finance & Risk Advisory
pulse_posts.title: The #1 Working Capital Mistake in Entry-Level Financial Modeling Tests
pulse_posts.body:
In 80% of financial analyst case interviews I grade, candidates link Net Income to the Cash Flow Statement properly but invert the cash impact of Accounts Receivable (AR) and Inventory.

Remember: an increase in an operating asset (AR or Inventory) is a CASH OUTFLOW, while an increase in Accounts Payable (AP) is a CASH INFLOW. Always run a balance sheet check row (Assets - Liabilities - Equity = 0) before submitting!

pulse_posts.mentor_headline: Executive Culinary Director & Kitchen Operations Specialist
pulse_posts.title: Mastering the Two-Stage Cooling Protocol & Station Mise en Place Under Rush Load
pulse_posts.body:
Whether you run a high-volume fast-food line or a brigade kitchen, two habits separate top operators from chaotic shifts:
1. Strict Temperature Danger Zone control (cooling cooked batches from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours, and down to 41°F within 4 hours).
2. FIFO (First-In, First-Out) pan rotation so prep waste stays under 3.5%.

questions.title: When should I use a CTE (WITH clause) versus a temporary indexed table in PostgreSQL?
questions.body: While doing the SQL micro-learning sprint, I noticed CTEs make complex aggregations readable, but how do they behave on multi-million row joins?

answers.body: Great question! Since PostgreSQL 12+, non-recursive CTEs referenced only once are inlined by default (acting like subqueries so index pushdown works). However, if a CTE is referenced multiple times and materialized in memory without indexes, a Temporary Table with an explicit CREATE INDEX on the join key is significantly faster for 5M+ rows.

questions.title: How do you justify WACC terminal growth rate assumptions during an valuation defense?
questions.body: If a company is growing revenue at 18% over the 5-year forecast window, why must the perpetuity growth rate (g) in the Gordon Growth Model stay below 2.5%–3.0%?

answers.mentor_headline: VP of Corporate Finance & Risk Advisory
answers.body: Because a terminal growth rate applies forever (to infinity). Mathematically, if a single firm grew faster than nominal global GDP (typically 2.5%–3.0%) forever, that single company would eventually become larger than the entire global economy. If the company still has high growth in Year 5, extend your explicit forecast to a 10-year two-stage DCF before applying terminal value.

questions.title: What is the exact corrective action if a hot-holding line drops below 135°F (57°C) during peak lunch?
questions.body: If our steam table thermometer reads 124°F during a rush check, can we just turn up the dial on the holding well, or do we have to reheat on the range?
questions.source_lesson_title: HACCP Critical Control Points in Commercial Kitchens

answers.mentor_headline: Executive Culinary Director & Kitchen Operations Specialist
answers.body: Never use a hot-holding steam table to reheat food! Holding wells are engineered only to maintain temperature, not bring food rapidly through the danger zone. Corrective action: If it has been under 135°F for less than 2 hours, rapidly reheat the batch on a stove/oven to 165°F (74°C) for at least 15 seconds before returning it to a verified 135°F+ holding well.
